decision.check: All visible faces, walls, rims and edges.
decision.defect_when: A localized corrosion pattern is visibly present on intact metal: mottled brown, orange, red, or rust-like discoloration accompanied by corrosion texture such as pitting, roughness, flaking, or an irregular oxidized patch. A single thin scratch, stain, dark line, or small isolated discoloration without corrosion texture is not corrosion.
decision.clear_when: No localized oxidized/corroded pattern with supporting corrosion texture is visible.
decision.review_when: Color or texture is too obscured to distinguish genuine oxidation/corrosion from a scratch, stain, finish variation, shadow, or normal surface texture.
ignore: Uniform plating/passivation tint.
Normal machining or polishing marks.
Thin scratches or linear surface marks without oxidation texture.
Small isolated discoloration without mottled corrosion texture.
Shadow without oxidation texture.
decision.boundary: Corrosion requires both a corrosion-like appearance and supporting surface texture; do not classify a generic brown/dark mark as corrosion. Missing material or a broken silhouette is edge_chip.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct corrosion patch.

decision.check: Sweep the complete visible surface and follow any candidate line end-to-end.
decision.defect_when: One thin, defined, continuous groove or line runs across a substantial distance of the surface. The groove may be bright, dark, bare-metal, or low-contrast; classify it from continuity and defined line-like geometry, not brightness alone.
decision.clear_when: Only normal grain, short polishing streaks, broad finish variation, or no continuous groove/line is visible.
decision.review_when: Glare, blur or occlusion prevents deciding whether a candidate line is continuous and defined.
ignore: Many short parallel finish-grain lines.
Broad specular gradients.
Diffuse shading or color variation without a defined continuous groove/line.
decision.boundary: A true continuous groove/line is line_mark regardless of whether it is bright or dark. A localized 3D depression is dent; a connected patch or smear without continuous groove geometry is dark_mark.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct line mark.

decision.check: Sweep faces, rims, edges, collars and flanges for contour changes.
decision.defect_when: Metal is pushed/deformed inward while material remains present, with a localized broken contour or depression.
decision.clear_when: The contour is intact and no localized 3D deformation is visible.
decision.review_when: There is not enough depth/contour evidence to distinguish deformation from a line or reflection.
ignore: Flat thin continuous bright lines.
Specular highlights on an intact contour.
decision.boundary: Missing material is edge_chip; a flat continuous groove is line_mark.
decision.localization: Tight box around each distinct dent/deformation.

decision.check: Trace the entire outer silhouette, rim and every flange/edge.
decision.defect_when: A notch, sheared break or chipped section shows material missing from an otherwise continuous silhouette.
decision.clear_when: The full visible silhouette is intact.
decision.review_when: The edge is cropped, blurred or obscured where a break may exist.
ignore: Reddish staining on an intact edge.
Pushed-in material with no missing section.
decision.boundary: Reddish oxidation on intact metal is corrosion; deformation without missing material is dent.
decision.localization: Tight box around each missing-material notch.

decision.check: Sweep the whole visible surface, every outer edge/rim and every hole/feature border.
decision.defect_when: A surface mark or patch is unmistakably very dark / near-black, with strong tonal contrast against the surrounding metal. Darkness is the primary defining characteristic. The feature may have any shape; it does not need to be connected, elongated, or patch-shaped.
decision.clear_when: No surface mark is unmistakably very dark / near-black with strong tonal contrast against the surrounding metal.
decision.review_when: The candidate feature is visible but glare, shadow, blur, exposure, or finish variation prevents deciding whether it is unmistakably very dark / near-black.
ignore: Rainbow/passivation tint that is not itself unmistakably very dark / near-black.
Hole bore or hole shadow.
Diffuse lighting gradients without a distinct surface mark.
A localized dark discoloration that is not unmistakably very dark / near-black; if otherwise reportable, that is dark_spot.
decision.boundary: Darkness is the primary defining characteristic of dark_mark. Use dark_mark when the surface feature is unmistakably very dark / near-black with strong tonal contrast, regardless of its shape. The same physical feature must never be reported as both dark_mark and dark_spot; if it qualifies as dark_mark, do not report that same feature as dark_spot.
decision.enumeration: Report every distinct physical dark_mark separately, with its own tight box.
decision.localization: Tight box around the actual very dark / near-black surface mark or patch, not the surrounding metal.

decision.check: Sweep the entire visible metal surface systematically, including the area around markings, holes, edges and transitions.
decision.defect_when: A localized dark discoloration or spot is visibly darker than the immediately surrounding metal and has a distinct footprint, but it is not unmistakably very dark / near-black or absolute-dark. It may be irregular, elongated, clustered, or otherwise non-uniform; shape does not make it a dark_mark when the darkness threshold is not met.
decision.clear_when: The inspected surface has no localized dark discoloration or spot that is reportable as dark_spot and is not unmistakably very dark / near-black.
decision.review_when: A localized dark feature is visible but resolution, glare, shadow, exposure, or finish variation prevents deciding whether it is a real dark discoloration or whether its darkness is unmistakably near-black.
ignore: Hole bore or hole shadow.
Uniform plating/passivation color.
Specular glare.
Diffuse lighting gradient without a bounded footprint.
Any feature that is unmistakably very dark / near-black; that feature belongs to dark_mark, not dark_spot.
decision.boundary: Use dark_spot for a localized dark discoloration or spot that is not unmistakably very dark / near-black. It may be irregular or clustered. Use dark_mark when darkness is unmistakably very dark / near-black with strong tonal contrast, regardless of shape. The same physical feature must never be reported as both dark_mark and dark_spot.
decision.enumeration: Report every distinct visible dark_spot separately; do not ignore a reportable spot merely because it is small, irregular, elongated, or clustered.
decision.localization: Tight box around the actual localized dark discoloration or spot, not the surrounding metal.

decision.check: Sweep the whole visible surface, edges/rims and feature borders.
decision.defect_when: A localized pale/dull low-luster patch contrasts with surrounding metal while underlying grain remains visible.
decision.clear_when: No localized dull/pale patch is present.
decision.review_when: Brightness and luster are too obscured to distinguish a dull patch from glare.
ignore: Specular highlight that is brighter and washes out grain.
Uniform overall finish tint.
decision.localization: Tight box around each localized dull/pale patch.
